cant play cause windows defender doesn't like it and im not going to make an exception in my defender profile for this game. 
It never launches just gets stuck and the pre launch with defender cycling reading files.  It  hasn't been patched and this is a very common problem according to AI so f em im uninstalling. They can support their POCr*p or not that's their business but I'm not playing it.

Great game but holy ♥♥♥♥ does this thing struggle to just want to launch at times. 
Also no internal game option to change the language.
Just because I live in an area that speaks French, does not mean I want my game in French! You gotta mess with the internal game files just to have it in english.

Continues from the last game the jaw-dropping lifelike graphics, excellent boss fights, and kickass combat. Highly encourage a playthrough to complete the trilogy.

Traveling through Arkham city in my opinion is rather slow and tedious. Especially during the segment of the game you have to disable penguin's signal disrupters. Because of that this is my least favorite Arkham batman game. It just makes progressing through the story a chore because of the world traversal.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the combat system is smoother, faster, and an improvement over the previous game.

citations.review_text:
[h1]Overall Score: 9.5/10[/h1]

[quote]So close to perfection. Almost a masterpiece.[/quote]

[hr][/hr]

[h2]The Good[/h2]

[list]
[*][b]Gameplay:[/b] Coming straight from Arkham Asylum, the combat feels drastically smoother with a wider variety of combos. Rocksteady made massive improvements here, it's a definitive upgrade.
[*][b]Visuals & Art Style:[/b] Shifts away from the creepy, isolated atmosphere of Asylum in favor of a richer, expanded art style. The new Batsuit design looks incredible too.
[*][b]Writing:[/b] Hands down the best story in the entire series!
[*][b]Villains:[/b] As evil as ever, but this time every villain plays an active, meaningful role in the main overarching narrative. 
[*][b]Open World:[/b] Expanding into an open city gives you complete freedom to explore, opening up whole new horizons. It feels great to navigate.
[*][b]Boss Fights:[/b] A massive step up from the previous game. Some fights really push you to your limits, forcing you to adapt and strategize to take them down.
[*][b]Companions:[/b] Getting to play as Catwoman and Robin is a very welcome addition that adds great variety.
[*][b]Gliding & Traversal:[/b] Gliding has much more depth and control. Traversal across the board feels significantly better.
[/list]

[hr][/hr]

[h2]The Bad[/h2]

[list]
[*][b]Riddler Trophies:[/b] Once again... quality over quantity, please!
[/list]

[hr][/hr]

[quote][b]Final Verdict:[/b] [i] Batman: Arkham City[/i] is an extraordinary step up from Asylum. You can feel the sheer amount of effort and passion the developers poured into every corner of this game.[/quote]

Now I understand why so many people love Batman: Arkham City. I have to say it's the best Arkham game I've ever played.

The story is fantastic. There are a lot of things going on, but it's easy to follow and has a great ending. I can't say too much about it because I don't want to spoil anything. Even though the game has been out for many years, there are still people who haven't played it.

The combat is a big improvement over Arkham Asylum. It's much faster, there are more enemies to fight, and Batman has a lot of fun gadgets to use. One issue I had, though, was that Batman would sometimes target the wrong enemy. It only happened a few times, but it was pretty annoying when it did. You can also play as Catwoman, Nightwing, and Robin. They all have their own unique combat styles and gadgets, which adds a lot of variety and makes the game even more fun.

There's also a ton of content, including Challenge Mode and Riddler collectibles. I actually think finding the Riddler trophies is harder in this game. I think it's because Arkham City has so many narrow walkways and densely packed areas filled with small details, making it easier to overlook them.

The atmosphere is incredible. I think the museum section has one of the best atmospheres I've ever experienced in a game. The giant exhibits and massive rooms create a creepy feeling. The city itself is also filled with dark corners and small environmental details that make it feel even more unsettling than Arkham Asylum.
Overall, I think Arkham City is the best Arkham game I've ever played. Now I completely understand why it's considered a classic. Next, I'm going to play Arkham Origins. I've heard it has some of the best boss fights in the series, so I'm looking forward to it.

10/10.

After finishing Batman: Arkham Asylum, I wasn't expecting much from Arkham City. My biggest issues with the previous game were how limited the combat eventually became and how clunky the overall movement felt. Fortunately, Arkham City immediately proved that Rocksteady understood those weaknesses and started refining the formula instead of simply repeating it.

The combat is where the improvement is most noticeable. It still follows the same Freeflow foundation, but everything feels smoother, more responsive and far less repetitive. Fights maintain a much better rhythm throughout the campaign, making combat genuinely enjoyable instead of becoming something you simply tolerate between story moments. It doesn't reinvent the system, but it improves it enough to make a significant difference.

The story kept me engaged from beginning to end, and I never felt that the main campaign overstayed its welcome. If anything, I actually appreciate that the core story doesn't drag on unnecessarily. The problem isn't the campaign itself, but everything surrounding it.

Arkham City offers plenty of optional content, but much of it feels designed to increase playtime rather than improve the overall experience. Missions like Victor Zsasz's phone calls quickly become repetitive, asking you to travel across the city over and over again without introducing anything mechanically interesting. The issue isn't that these missions are optional. The issue is that many of them rely on repeating the same gameplay loop while sending you back and forth across the map.

That leads to another problem: traversal. While opening the game into Arkham City was a natural evolution from the confined areas of Arkham Asylum, moving around the city never feels particularly satisfying. Long distances become noticeable because Batman's mobility is still fairly limited compared to what the series would eventually achieve. claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features multiple playable characters, including Catwoman, Robin, and Nightwing, each with unique move sets.

citations.review_text:
Good:
‣ The story is better than Asylum imo, but it has bad pacing. Expecting Batman to fight so many villains in such a short span feels like too much, and it loses its focus. Even with that, I still found the story and side stories pretty entertaining.
‣ Most characters are interesting, and compared to Asylum, I think Batman doesn't feel boring or flat. His personality and ideals are shown more through his actions, speech, and remarks.
‣ Maintains the "dark & gritty" art direction from the prequel and looks a little more pleasing.
‣ Multiple playable characters with unique combat sets (Batman, Catwoman, Robin, Nightwing).
                                        ^ Fun combat overall
‣ Has NG+.
‣ New costumes after finishing the main story.

Mixed:
‣ The last boss fight in the main story was quite lame and boring.
‣ Bigger map and easy to learn, but it has a really weird shape.
‣ Lots of gadgets to use, but they don't feel intuitive to use and access. 
‣ Stealth feels really repetitive and makes it easy. Either go behind/above/under.

Bad:
‣ Sometimes crashes when alt-tabbing.
‣ Sometimes tedious side quests (gameplay wise, story wise most of them were pretty good). Go there, scan that, follow that, wait, etc.
‣ Lots of collectible items.
‣ Augment Reality Training: Failed.

Conclusion:
   With all this said, i found Batman Arkham City to be better than Asylium, but as it's separate thing it's not a masterpiece or a hidden gem, it's just a decent game with plenty of content, but it's not something I'd recommend paying full price for especially when it goes in sale quite frequently.

citations.review_text: One of the best superhero game ever made, truly an upgrade from Asylum in every way, story is fantastic, combat feels smoother, side quests were also really great and weren't long or annoying (except, well.... Riddler's), catwoman's part was also really good although I felt like it was a bit short, Harley's DLC was also fun, playing as Robin was cool, but Achievements were really hard I hate Riddler ong.....

Batman Arkham City is truly a masterpiece. This game really makes you feel like Batman. The storyline, game mechanics, and character designs are all perfect.

The Boss Fights are not that difficult. Collecting The Riddler Trophies is again time consuming if you want to finish the game 100% . Beside the Story Mode, The Riddler Revenge Challenges are more trickier and harder than the Challenges in Batman Arkham Asylum.

The Thugs' dialogues are hilarious. "It's The Freakin Bat!" dialogue is one of my favourite dialogues. Playing other characters aside from Batman is also pretty good. This game is definitely worth playing.

If you're a sadistic and want to feel like batman then play this game normally. If you're a masochist, 100% the game. I love the game, but the achievements made me felt like I was a psychiatric patient held contained in a highly secured asylum except it's no asylum but a game set in a city and I'm a free bird in an open cage. 

8.5/10, wouldn't 100% it again, but It's fun in the worst and best way possible.

One of the best "git gud" games I've played and definitely deserves the overwhelmingly positive ratings.

Better graphics than the original.

Animations are very well done and combat flows like water once you master it.

Finding all the collectables was both a chore and rewarding at the same time as you need the XP to get upgrades for Batman. The Riddler challenges and campaign though.. This is not fun. To get a couple of achievements, they make you grind your soul away. It becomes an unbearable slog.

The atmosphere is dark and fits perfectly with a Batman game.

Sounds are great.
Music is great and fits with the game and atmosphere.

Better in every aspect than the previous game.

Possibly one of the best Arkham bat man games in the series and worth playing to it's "ALMOST" fullest. The combat, stealth and overall gameplay is great. 

An after all these years the game still runs very smooth with little to no crashes just like the day it was released 

But for anyone who's a completionist i can not recommend for some of the challenges this game makes you do....It's possible but by the end of it you will view this wonderful game as a hellish punishment. Just play the story and get all riddler trophies if you want to get a completion feel out of it. After getting all the achievements in the game my fingers felt numb...i would rather get my balls cheese gratered than get all the achievements in the game.

This game is a gem, it is a game that is the best example of a sequel, the combat, story, characters, and everything in between is amazing. I do have to say if you are a completionist like 100% all steam trophies then you not going to have a good time, once I finished all Riddlers revenge I wanted to kill Riddler and than kill myself, this trophy 100% is horrible. But the game is a solid 8/10. The major thing that I loved about this game was how they expanded upon the combat, In the first game most attacks like stun, batclaw, bataranges did not have any reason to be used during combat, but in city every single form of attack has a purpose, the gadgets are useful, the stun is useful and it feels so much more fun to combo enemies with these set new moves, unfortunately they did get rid of the throw. I do also miss the goofy nature and simple gameplay of the first game.
Thank you for reading and take care.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the combat system was expanded with new moves while existing moves and controls were improved and given distinct purposes.

citations.review_text: A great sequel to a revolutionary Superhero game, Arkham City improves on everything Arkham Asylum was built on and makes it twice as better. Felt like the asylum was too small? You get thrown into a part of Gotham City now, with many of its sections being controlled by many supervillains. The combat and stealth are also way better, with many new moves being added and existing moves being improved. Kevin Conroy (R.I.P) and Mark Hamill are also back as their respective roles of Batman and The Joker.

They took everything from [b]Batman: Arkham Asylum[/b] and improved on it in what I would call the perfect, logical next step.  The combat is expanded.  The map is expanded.  The roster is expanded.  The metroidvania aspects I praised in the first game take a bit of a back seat, but they're still present.

Everything you learned about stealth and combat in the previous game still applies here.  All of your muscle memory carries over.  The developers did that perfect thing where they looked at the controller, looked at which button combinations weren't being used, and gave them a purpose.  None of the existing controls were broken or replaced.  They simply added more options.  On top of that, they gradually introduce new enemy types throughout the game, forcing you to incorporate those new abilities into your toolkit.

The map is significantly larger, but like the first game, they still manage to make every corner interesting without making it feel bloated.  There are no large, empty expanses that exist solely to fill space.  Riddler challenges return and are scattered throughout the city.  They've also added proper side quests that give landmarks and districts a purpose beyond simply passing through them.  Even after the story ends, goons continue to respawn in various locations, giving exploration and combat some life in the post-game.

Not knowing how successful the first game would become, the developers were right to use Joker immediately in [b]Arkham Asylum[/b].  That meant they needed a different approach for the sequel, and Dr. Strange was a great choice not used much in other media.  Like the first game, [b]Arkham City[/b] tells a strong Batman ensemble story.  Penguin, Ra's al Ghul, and Mr. Freeze all play major roles, but none of them feel shoehorned into the narrative.  Every villain serves a purpose, and every subplot feels like part of the same larger story.

Batman Arkham City is probably one of the best superhero games in the world. Everything that made Arkham Asylum great was made greater in Arkham City, and everything that made Arkham Asylum bad was improved upon. The music is FANTASTIC. The gameplay is AMAZING. The traversal is STELLAR And the combat. The combat is GLORIOUS> More characters. More map. More story. To quote Homelander. "I gotta tell you. It was perfect. Perfect. Everything down to the last minute details." If I was to rate this game out of 10. I'd give it a 50. Well worth the price of purchase, and well worth the hours spent playing. 

Put it like this. I have played this game on the PS3, Xbox360 and PC. And not just once each. A multitude of times.
